text:
maya: Ran a full nsys + perfetto pass on the 512-batch ramp scenario (nightly). Seeing a ~450-700ms tail on first token for several model variants. Suspect JIT/cache churn rather than pure kernel slowness.

oliver: Can you paste the nsys command you used?

maya: `nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt -f true --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- python run_ramp.py --batches 512`

maya: Perfetto timeline: big clustered sections labeled "triton_jit_compile" on device stream 0, interleaved with short exec kernels. The compile blocks are ~60-180ms each and they happen on-path for first requests after scale-up. Link: https://perfetto.local/trace/XXXX (redacted)

sasha: Do we have numbers for how often compile hits vs cache hits?

maya: From logs: for model v2.1.4 we observe ~23 compile ops in the first 120s window, cache hit ratio ~0.67 -> so ~1/3 cold. For v2.2.0 hit ratio improves to 0.82. But the interesting bit: compile ops correlate with batches that contain longer-seq requests (seq_len>1024).

tony: Could KV cache eviction policy be evicting entries for longer sequences and forcing recompile of fused kernels?

maya: Possibly. Perfetto shows KV cache warm-up sequences then a spike of "kv_populate" followed by immediate compile calls. Looks like prefix caching causes different kernel selection path.

oliver: Any CPU-side stalls? nsys should show cpu-gpu timeline.

maya: Yes — big CPU wait states on the worker that handles routing. There's repeated host->device memcpy peaks just before compile entries. nvprof-esque counters: `cudaLaunchTime` ~12-20ms per small kernel, but the compile entries are pure device-side JIT time.

perf-bot: automated note: collected kernel list and sizes -> saved as /artifacts/jit-kernel-list-1812345678.json

sasha: Could the batching heuristic be merging requests with disparate seq lengths causing de-opt paths?

maya: That's my current hypothesis. Example: when short (128) and long (2048) are co-batched, runtime chooses a specialized kernel for long seq, triggers a fallback compile for mixed-case fusion, and we miss the cached variant.

tony: Repro steps to validate?

maya: 1) replay perf trace with only homogeneous sequences (all 128) -> no compile spikes.
 2) replay with interleaved short+long -> compile spikes reproduce.
 3) force `TRITON_JIT_CACHE_DIR` to empty to simulate cold cache -> amplifies the effect.

oliver: Can we add a metric to the Console: `jit_compile_count` per model+version and `kcache_miss_rate`?

sasha: yes, add those to the runtime telemetry consumer. We'll surface as histograms per model shard.

maya: One more interesting find: when we enable `async_jit_compiler=true` the host-side stalls drop but device time increases slightly; latency tail improves in p95 but p99 still hit ~3x baseline in cold starts. So async helps throughput but doesn't eliminate compile cost.

tony: Thoughts on mitigation roadmap?

oliver: Short/medium term: 1) tweak batching heuristic to avoid mixing >2x sequence length ratio, 2) pre-warm common kernel variants during scale-up (background), 3) expose a flag to pin kernel variant per model to disable on-the-fly compile.

sasha: Long term: 1) persistent kernel cache on shared NVMe with eviction policy tuned for prefix-kv patterns, 2) compile-ahead profiling: sample incoming seq distribution and precompile top-K variants during off-peak.

maya: I'll open a PR to add jit_compile_count/kcache_miss_rate to telemetry and a dashboard. Also adding a small reproducer in perf tests that mixes seq lengths to ensure we catch regressions.

oliver: Please also attach perfetto slices (exported png) and the nsys .qdrep to the issue. We need a triage doc for SRE on how to interpret these compile spikes.

maya: Uploaded artifacts to /artifacts/eng-runtime/jit-churn/1812345678/: `trace.qdrep`, `perfetto.json`, `kernel-timeline.txt`, `kcache-stats.csv`.

tony: Quick check: are we seeing any memory pressure on device right before compile? Could memory allocs cause fragmentation leading to slow compile paths?

maya: GPU memory free drops ~200MB before compile, but not OOM-level. Still, fragmentation might change allocator path used during JIT, adding overhead. Adding malloc/free instrumentation to the run.

sasha: Good. Also, add unit test for batching heuristic that forbids mixes >4x seq ratio by default and a flag to relax.

oliver: Final ask: mark this as P2 regression for now and add to next eng-runtime sprint. Assign to maya + sasha.

maya: Ack. I'll create the issue and link reproducer + perf traces.

perf-bot: Incident template: https://redwood.internal/incidents/new?template=perf-jit-churn (auto-populated).

maya: Thanks all. I'll update the thread when I have dashboard and PR links. :thumbsup:
